text:
You need a proof-of-concept chatbot that feels human-like, verifies a patient’s identity, checks appointment availability from a database, books the slot, and sends an SMS confirmation.

I’ve built conversational assistants in Python that connect language models to real workflows, and I can help you shape this POC into a clean end-to-end flow for doctors or clinics. For the booking scenario, I would keep the experience focused on a few reliable steps: greet the user, collect and verify the needed identity fields, check the appointment database, present available slots, confirm the chosen time, and trigger the SMS confirmation after booking. Since this is a POC, the priority should be accuracy, predictable conversation flow, and a natural tone rather than overcomplicating the design.

A relevant project is my Delivery support chatbot for Parcelwise Logistics (p09). I built a WhatsApp and SMS assistant using Python, OpenAI API, LangGraph, FastAPI, Redis, and Twilio that tracks parcels, reschedules deliveries, and hands off to a human with full context. One result from that work was that 43% of conversations were resolved without an agent. That experience is directly useful here because your use case also needs guided conversation, database-backed actions, and SMS messaging.

I also built a Contract clause search assistant (p05) for a confidential legal client using Python, LangChain, OpenAI API, pgvector, PostgreSQL, and FastAPI. It answered questions over 9,000 contracts and always quoted the clause and page it used. One result was reducing clause lookup from 25 minutes to 3 minutes. That project strengthened my approach to grounding responses in data and keeping the assistant precise, which matters for patient identity checks and appointment details.

With 6 years of experience in Python, machine learning, NLP, PyTorch, scikit-learn, LangChain, OpenAI API, Hugging Face Transformers, XGBoost, and pandas, I can help you build the POC in a practical way and keep the implementation straightforward.

Would you like the assistant to handle only one clinic database at first, or should it be designed from the start to support multiple doctors and locations?
